report.summary: Read daedalus/eval/mint.py chunk 3 of 3 (lines 561-720). Enumerated symbols and claims; found no broken claims.

handoff.purpose: Final chunk: task construction, diagnostics logging, landed-edit and commit minting, confirmation, persistence.

symbols.name: _log_mint_diagnostics
symbols.note: Logs skipped out-of-scope files and no-task reason via _LOG.info; returns None.

symbols.name: mint_task_from_landed_edit
symbols.note: Mints one quarantined task from report['wrote']; returns None if no task.

symbols.name: mint_from_commit
symbols.note: Mints tasks from a git commit; returns list (currently one task or empty).

symbols.name: confirm_task
symbols.note: Increments confirmations and promotes tier to primary at threshold; mutates dict in place.

symbols.name: load_minted_tasks
symbols.note: Reads JSON mint store; returns [] if missing; sorts by id.

symbols.name: save_minted_tasks
symbols.note: Writes JSON store with sorted keys and tasks sorted by id; returns path.

symbols.name: add_minted_task
symbols.note: Upserts one task by id into store; returns path.

symbols.name: confirm_minted_task
symbols.note: Confirms one task by id, persists, returns updated task or None.

claims.text: The "reported, never silent" channel for information that doesn't fit the two public mint_* entry points' pre-existing dict | None / list[dict] return shape ... A task that DID mint carries its own skipped_out_of_scope/must_include_dropped fields; this is what surfaces the same information -- and the no-task-minted reason -- for the cases where there is no task dict to carry it.
claims.why: Function logs skipped_out_of_scope and reason via _LOG.info; the task dict carries skipped_out_of_scope and must_include_dropped fields in the task construction above. No contradiction.

claims.text: report["wrote"] IS disk_changed from offload.py:194-197 -- the files that ACTUALLY changed on disk, found by diffing a before/after content-hash snapshot taken around the run. That is the independent oracle here; the model's self-reported files_changed is deliberately not read
claims.why: The claim references offload.py internals and the model's report fields; this chunk only reads report.get("wrote") and does not verify that it is a content-hash diff. The behavior of offload.py is outside this chunk.

claims.text: The edit is assumed uncommitted (offload writes straight into the working tree and never commits): "before" is read from git HEAD, "after" from the file currently on disk.
claims.why: The code calls _show(repo_root, "HEAD", rel) for before and _read_worktree(repo_root, rel) for after, matching the claim.

claims.text: A file the run created has no HEAD blob (before = None); a file it deleted has nothing left on disk (after = None).
claims.why: before is set to _show(...) only if sha is truthy, otherwise None; after is _read_worktree(...) which can return None for a missing file. The mapping stores those values directly.

claims.text: Returns None if there is nothing to mint: no writes reported, every write's content is symbol-identical to HEAD (e.g. a formatting-only touch this diff granularity can't see through), no written file is in the project's index scope, or only one in-scope file has a diffed symbol (no cross-file label exists -- see the module docstring's CROSS-FILE ONLY rule).
claims.why: The function returns None if _mint_from_diffs yields no task, but the specific reasons (symbol-identical, out-of-scope, single-file) are implemented in _mint_from_diffs, which is not in this chunk. The early return for no writes is present.

claims.text: Same idea as mint_task_from_landed_edit, but against history that already exists -- this is what lets minting be exercised deterministically in tests without a live offload run (a temp git fixture IS real git history; git show gives exact before/after text with no mocking).
claims.why: The function uses _git diff-tree and _show to obtain before/after text from real git history; no mocking is visible. The claim about test determinism is consistent with the code.

claims.text: Currently mints a single aggregate task per commit (via the same _mint_from_diffs used for landed edits); returns a list so a future split (e.g. one task per hunk, for very large commits) is additive rather than a signature change.
claims.why: The function calls _mint_from_diffs once and returns [task] if task else [], producing a single task per commit.

claims.text: Returns [] for an unresolvable ref, a commit that touches no in-scope file, or one where only a single in-scope file has a diffed symbol (no cross-file label exists) -- never raises.
claims.why: The unresolvable ref case is handled (returns [] if not full_sha). The in-scope and single-file cases are decided inside _mint_from_diffs, not visible here. The 'never raises' claim is plausible but the function calls _git and _resolve_sha which could raise; however, the claim is about the function's own behavior and the code has no try/except, so the verdict is UNCHECKABLE because the called helpers' behavior is not in this chunk.

claims.text: --root: a commit with no parent (the very first commit of history) is diffed against the empty tree instead of silently producing no rows. No-op for every other commit (it already has a parent to diff against).
claims.why: The code passes --root to diff-tree and computes parent via f"{full_sha}^" which resolves to None for a root commit; then before is None and after is shown from full_sha, matching the comment.

claims.text: Record one independent confirmation of a minted task, in place.
claims.why: The function mutates task['confirmations'] and task['tier'] directly.

claims.text: Promotes task["tier"] from "quarantine" to "primary" once confirmations reaches MINT_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD.
claims.why: The code checks tier == 'quarantine', increments confirmations, and sets tier to 'primary' when confirmations >= MINT_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD.

claims.text: A no-op on a task that is not currently quarantined: a primary task doesn't need more confirming, and "confirming" a hand_reachable task is meaningless -- it was never gated in the first place.
claims.why: The function returns task immediately if tier != 'quarantine'.

claims.text: Returns the same (mutated) dict for convenient chaining; callers that need the pre-mutation task should copy it first.
claims.why: The function returns the same dict object it received.

claims.text: Read the persisted mint store, or [] if it does not exist yet.
claims.why: The function returns [] if os.path.exists(p) is false.

claims.text: This is the ONLY load path by which a minted task can reach daedalus.eval.harness.all_tasks() and therefore any go/no-go number -- without it, mint_task_from_landed_edit/mint_from_commit produced dicts that lived only as long as the caller's local variable.
claims.why: The claim about harness.all_tasks() and the uniqueness of this load path depends on code outside this chunk; the function itself only reads the store.

claims.text: Sorted by id for deterministic iteration (PYTHONHASHSEED-independent), matching the rest of this repo's output-determinism rule.
claims.why: The function returns sorted(data.get('tasks', []), key=lambda t: t['id']).

claims.text: Overwrite the mint store with exactly tasks. Deterministic formatting (sorted keys, sorted by id) so the diff is meaningful in review -- same contract as harness.write_baseline. Returns the path written.
claims.why: The function writes json.dump with sort_keys=True, indent=2, and sorts tasks by id; returns p.

claims.text: Persist task into the mint store, keyed by id. Idempotent: minting the same diff twice (same target + same must_include, via the content hash in _mint_from_diffs) yields the same id and overwrites in place rather than duplicating -- re-running a mint (e.g. after a rebase that reproduces an identical patch) must not inflate the quarantine count.
claims.why: The function builds a dict keyed by task['id'] and overwrites the existing entry; the id derivation is in _mint_from_diffs (not visible) but the overwrite behavior is implemented here.

claims.text: Load the store, confirm ONE task by id (see confirm_task), persist the mutation, and return the updated task -- or None if task_id is not in the store.
claims.why: The function loads tasks, finds the matching id, calls confirm_task(t), saves, and returns t; returns None if not found.

claims.text: The only durable way a quarantined mint accumulates confirmations and eventually promotes to primary; confirm_task alone only mutates an in-memory dict that would otherwise evaporate.
claims.why: confirm_minted_task persists via save_minted_tasks, while confirm_task only mutates in memory. The claim about durability is supported by the code.

observations.what: mint_from_commit computes parent as f"{full_sha}^" and passes it to _show; for a root commit parent is None, so before is None. This matches the comment.

confirm_minted_task mutates the task dict in the loaded list and then saves the whole list; if save fails, the in-memory dict is mutated but not persisted, but the function does not handle save errors.

load_minted_tasks assumes the JSON has a 'tasks' key; if the file is malformed or has a different shape, json.load raises and the function propagates. The docstring says 'or [] if it does not exist yet' but does not claim to handle corrupt files.
save_minted_tasks writes with sort_keys=True and indent=2, ensuring deterministic output; the trailing newline is added explicitly.
